definition: The comparative method is an approach that studies different peoples, times, or conditions side by side to trace relationships, movements, and the development and direction of customs, beliefs, and thought-habits. In anthropology, it is used both to show broad resemblances and important differences across human activities and to connect surviving or recorded practices with evidence from earlier societies.
